exposure: Expectant management of Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP)
Presence or absence of a visible niche on first-trimester transvaginal ultrasonography
cohort: The study included 54 pregnant women diagnosed with Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) in the first trimester who underwent expectant management.
finding: Patients with a visible niche on sonography were significantly more likely to experience adverse obstetric outcomes, including preterm labor, placenta accreta spectrum, placenta previa, low-birth-weight newborns, and severe delivery complications.
